title: 1. Data Processing
text: best case scenario, survey data collected format preserves metadata survey, variable labels value labels. often case data collected using YouGov’s Gryphon software solutions like Quantilope, Qualtrics SurveyMonkey, can export data formats retain information, commonly SPSS .sav files. case, names variables (e.g. “F600”) values (e.g. “1”, “2”, “3”) preserved, also labels describe variables values represent: Variable labels: provide human-readable description variable represents. example, variable named “F600” might label like “Wie attraktiv finden Sie die BKW als Arbeitgeberin?”, makes clear question participants answered. Value labels: provide human-readable description value represents. example, value “1” variable “F600” might label like “1 - Überhaupt nicht attraktiv”, makes clear response option participants. import labelled dataset R using haven::read_sav() function, can easily access variable labels value labels. YouAnalyser package provides functions work metadata, allowing quickly understand analyze survey data without manually decode variable value names. different ways can inspect variable value labels R, e.g.: YouAnalyser provides dp_inspect_codebook() function print codebook labelled data console, includes variable labels value labels tidy format:

text: kda_regression() function main work horse conducting KDA. wrapper function necessary steps (subfunctions) conduct KDA, including fitting regression model, calculating variable importance performance measures, creating relevant plots. function several arguments allow customize analysis, choice regression model, variable importance method, diagnostic options. can get help function arguments running help("kda_regression") ?kda_regression R console. need provide least following arguments kda_regression() function: data: data frame containing outcome predictors. data needs haven::labelled() format, typically case SPSS data. , refer vignette("dp", package = "YouAnalyser") vignette Data Processing convert data labelled format. outcome: single string naming outcome variable. predictors: character vector predictor variable names. can use e.g. paste0("F800_", 1:8) specify sequence variables similar names. Option 2: model: Instead providing data, outcome, predictors arguments, can also directly provide fitted regression model object lm() glm() model argument (intended advanced users.) kda_regression() function also several options. recommended default values need changed cases: diagnostics = FALSE: logical indicating whether compute model diagnostics. necessary KDA , can useful checking assumptions regression model. set TRUE, diagnostic plots included output. importance_method = "auto": method calculate variable importance. default “auto” conduct dominance analysis number predictors less 15. Otherwise, use “jrw” method, computationally efficient method calculating variable importance larger models. See information available variable importance methods. importance_barPlots_args = list(): list additional arguments passed importance bar plot function. See kda_importance_barPlot() details. performance_barPlot_args = list(): list additional arguments passed performance bar plot function. See kda_performance_barPlot() details. ipma_scatterPlot_args = list(): list additional arguments passed IPMA scatter plot function. See kda_ipma_scatterPlot() details. title: 3. Key Driver Analysis
text: three methods available calculating variable importance kda_regression() function: "domir" Dominance Analysis: method decomposes R-squared regression model contributions predictor variable. provides comprehensive measure variable importance can computationally intensive models many predictors. method also known Relative Importance, LMG Shapley Value Decomposition. "jrw" Johnson Relative Weights: Similarly dominance analysis, method decomposes R-squared regression model contributions predictor variable. However, using heuristic method computationally efficient can handle models larger number predictors. "sumOfCoefficients" Sum Absolute (Standardized) Coefficients: method calculates variable importance taking sum absolute values (standardized) regression coefficients predictor variable. simpler computationally efficient method, account intercorrelations predictors may provide accurate measure variable importance two methods. included legacy reasons recommended use cases. Note default method set "auto", automatically choose "domir" "jrw" based number predictors model. fewer 15 predictors, use "domir". 15 predictors, use "jrw". Set importance_method argument one three methods override default behavior specify method directly. extended discussion Dominance Analysis Johnson Relative Weights methods, please refer subsections end vignette. inteded interested readers reference clients want know methods used KDA. additional ressources, please refer following resources: Vignette domir package: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/domir/vignettes/domir_basics.html Technical paper Dominance Analysis Method: Grömping, Ulrike. 2007. Estimators Relative Importance Linear Regression Based Variance Decomposition. American Statistician 61 (2): 139–47. https://doi.org/10.1198/000313007X188252. Technical paper Johnson Relative Weights Method: Johnson, J. (2000). heuristic method estimating relative weight predictor variables multiple regression. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 35, 1–19 . https://doi.org/10.1207/S15327906MBR3501_1

However, general guideline, often recommended least 10-15 observations per predictor variable model reliable estimation. Therefore, model 14 predictors, ideally want least 140-210 observations subgroup ensure stable interpretable results.

what: 1.1 The Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter
title: 4. Price Sensitivity Meter
text: Price Sensitivity Meter (PSM), developed Peter van Westendorp, direct, survey-based technique estimating range prices consumers find acceptable product concept. main appeal can used product exists market, e.g. new product concept repositioning, historical sales pricing data rely . respondent asked four open-ended price questions product concept: cheap: “price consider Product X priced low feel quality couldn’t good?” Cheap: “price consider Product X bargain - great buy money?” Expensive: “price consider Product X starting get expensive, question, give thought buying ?” expensive: “price consider Product X expensive consider buying ?” Plotting cumulative distribution four answers price yields four curves whose intersections used derive key PSM reference points: IDP (Indifference Price Point): intersection “cheap” “expensive” - price equal shares respondents see product cheap versus expensive. can interpreted price market “expects” product. OPP (Optimal Price Point): intersection “cheap” “expensive” - price minimizes share respondents rejecting product either quality-suspicion (cheap) cost (expensive) grounds. Acceptable price range: bounded intersection “cheap” “cheap”, intersection “expensive” “expensive”. PSM good fit whenever need quick, inexpensive read acceptable pricing bounds early product development. main limitation follows directly measures: bounds acceptability, says nothing many people actually buy given price, implies revenue.

title: 4. Price Sensitivity Meter
text: Newton-Miller-Smith (NMS) extension closes gap adding two purchase-intent questions, piping respondent’s answer basic PSM questions: “likely purchase Product X [piped: price given cheap]?” (1: extremely unlikely - 5: extremely likely) “likely purchase Product X [piped: price given expensive]?” (1: extremely unlikely - 5: extremely likely) lets move plausible price range (PSM) concrete price recommendations: price maximizes reach (market penetration) price maximizes revenue, often price. Use NMS extension whenever can afford two additional questions need kind actionable pricing guidance rather just acceptable range.

Starting k initial centres, alternates assigning respondent nearest centre recomputing centre mean members, assignment longer changes. result set compact clusters small WSS. weakness: result depends randomly chosen initial centres. Hierarchical clustering Ward’s method (Ward, 1963) starts respondent cluster successively merges two clusters whose merger increases WSS least, respondents one cluster. result tree (dendrogram) can cut number clusters. weakness: merged, respondents change cluster, even fit better elsewhere. Hierarchical k-means (Kassambara, 2017) first runs hierarchical clustering, cuts tree k clusters, uses centres clusters starting centres k-means, optimizes assignment. result deterministic (random starts) combines global view hierarchical clustering optimization k-means.

what: 1. Data Processing, Convenience Functions, and Example Data

text: data processing functions start prefix dp_, convenience functions start prefix ya_. detailed walkthrough data processing functions, please refer vignette included package (use e.g. vignette("dp", package = "YouAnalyser")), provide step--step guides use various functions data processing convenient tasks. YouAnalyser assumes data comes haven::labelled() format, common survey data. package includes functions help process prepare data analysis data already format: dp_copy_codebook_template(): Copy codebook template specified file path dp_convert_to_labelled(): Convert data frame labelled data frame using codebook. dp_label_automatically(): Automatically label data frame based values (useful filling missing labels want use dp_convert_to_labelled() codebook - use caution!) dp_inspect_codebook(): Inspect codebook labelled data frame (useful check whether labelling worked expected) dp_zap_missings(): Remove missing values value labels labelled data frame. convenience functions starting ya_ mostly take care selecting files, defining file names, saving plots: ya_choose_file(): Choose existing file return path ya_choose_file_path(): Choose existing directory define new file directory, returning full file path ya_save_plot(): Save plot JPEG Special consideration given ya_setup_folder_structure(), creates standardized folder structure project. function designed help organize files outputs consistent way across different projects. default, creates following folder structure: make_rproj = TRUE, folder also set RStudio project. template, template script analysis copied 02_scripts: "kda" Key Driver Analysis (see vignette("kda", package = "YouAnalyser")) "seg" segmentation (see vignette("seg", package = "YouAnalyser")), e.g. ya_setup_folder_structure("mySegmentation", template = "seg").

title: Provide Standardized Analytics Products for YouGov DACH
text: PSM functions start prefix psm_. perform Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter analysis, including Newton-Miller-Smith (NMS) extension, export results standardized reporting templates. detailed walkthrough, please refer vignette("psm", package = "YouAnalyser"). psm_analysis() psm_analysis_weighted(): Run (unweighted weighted) Van Westendorp analysis (re-exported pricesensitivitymeter package). psm_design_for_weighted(): Build survey design psm_analysis_weighted() weight variable. psm_plot(): Plot price sensitivity curves price points acceptable price range, plus reach revenue plots NMS extension. psm_save_data_for_chart() psm_copy_pptx_template(): Export results Excel PowerPoint templates.

title: Provide Standardized Analytics Products for YouGov DACH
text: segmentation functions start prefix seg_. cover complete segmentation (cluster analysis) survey data. detailed walkthrough, including interpretation metrics, please refer vignette("seg", package = "YouAnalyser"). template script segmentation project available ya_setup_folder_structure(template = "seg"). seg_prep_data(): Prepare clustering variables (missing values, rescaling) compute distance matrix. seg_clustering_tendency(): Check whether data contains meaningful clusters . seg_optimal_clusters(): Suggest number clusters (elbow method, silhouette, gap statistic, NbClust). seg_compare_algorithms(): Compare clustering algorithms numbers clusters. seg_cluster(): Run cluster analysis (hierarchical k-means default, many algorithms) standardized results plots. seg_validation() seg_agreement(): Validate solutions internal external measures, compare solutions different algorithms. seg_plot_centers(): Plot profiles clusters. predict(): Assign new respondents (e.g. new wave) clusters. clusters can described detail eda_ functions, conveniently interactive app eda_explore().

Defaults "pearson". correlation_args Optional. list additional arguments passed correlation::correlation(). ggcorr_args Optional. list arguments passed GGally::ggcorr().

what: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
title: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
text: Computes descriptive statistics several variables , optionally group (e.g. cluster solution) weighted. Numeric variables summarized mean, standard deviation, standard error, confidence interval quantiles; categorical variables (weighted) frequency distribution, using value labels.

title: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
code: eda_describe(   data,   vars,   group = NULL,   weight = NULL,   treat_as = c("auto", "numeric", "categorical"),   conf_level = 0.95,   total = FALSE,   test = FALSE,   test_method = c("parametric", "nonparametric"),   reference = c("total", "rest", "meandev", "groups"),   p_adjust = "holm",   min_labels = 5 )

title: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
text: data data frame, typically haven-labelled tibble, output seg_cluster() (see "Grouping cluster solution"). vars variables describe: character vector names tidyselect expression, e.g. dplyr::starts_with("F50_0_"). group Optional. Name grouping variable (e.g. "cluster_k4"). Respondents missing group excluded. weight Optional. Name weight variable. treat_as "auto" (default), "numeric" "categorical". See "Numeric categorical?". conf_level Confidence level confidence intervals. Defaults 0.95. total TRUE group given, "Total" group respondents added. Defaults FALSE. test TRUE group given, group differences tested eda_test(). Defaults FALSE. test_method "parametric" (default) "nonparametric", passed eda_test(). reference Reference comparisons groups, passed eda_test(): "total" (default, group vs. total including group), "rest" (group vs. rest sample), "meandev" (group vs. mean group means) "groups" (pairs groups). See eda_test(), "Statistical tests", details. p_adjust Method adjust p-values comparisons (see stats::p.adjust()). Defaults "holm". min_labels Minimum number value labels distinct values variable treated numeric (treat_as = "auto"). Defaults 5.

title: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
text: object class eda_describe, list elements: numeric: tibble one row per numeric variable (group): n (valid answers), n_eff (effective sample size, weighted), missing, mean, sd, se, ci_low, ci_high, median, q1, q3, min, max. NULL numeric variables. categorical: tibble one row per categorical variable, (group) category: n (unweighted count), n_weighted percent (weighted share among valid answers, 0-100). NULL categorical variables. tests: eda_test() results test = TRUE, otherwise NULL. settings: list settings used.

title: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
text: treat_as = "auto", variable summarized numeric (means) least min_labels value labels (e.g. 5-point Likert scale), least min_labels distinct observed values (e.g. 1-10 scale labelled end points ) value labels . Factors, character vectors labelled variables fewer values summarized categorical (frequency distributions). Use treat_as = "numeric" "categorical" treat variables way.

title: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
text: User-defined missing values (e.g. "know" = 99, kept haven::read_sav(user_na = TRUE)) set NA computing statistic, never distort means percentages.

title: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
text: weight given, means, standard deviations, quantiles percentages weighted. Standard errors confidence intervals use effective sample size Kish, \(n_{eff} = (\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\), accounts loss precision due weighting (reported n_eff).

title: Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables — eda_describe
text: data can also output seg_cluster() (seg_cluster seg_cluster_set). original data (data_full, variables labels, restricted clustered respondents) used, cluster solution added labelled grouping variable, e.g. cluster_k4 (noise points density-based methods labelled "Noise").

title: Explore data interactively — eda_explore
text: Opens Shiny gadget (viewer pane default) explore variables data set: select variables name label (pattern, e.g. whole item battery), choose grouping variable (e.g. cluster solution) optional weight, get plots selected variables one plot (eda_plot()): horizontal vertical bar charts means without error bars, boxplots, stacked bar charts distributions; descriptive statistics (eda_describe()); tests group differences (eda_test(), see "Statistical tests" ), comparing group total (default), rest sample, mean group means, groups; ggstatsplot installed, detailed plot single variable test results (eda_plot_detail(); "Detailed plot" tab, customizable sidebar); codebook variable value labels; code reproduce plot statistics script. plots can downloaded JPEG (ya_save_plot(), 300 dpi) statistics Excel file. Click "Done" close gadget return console.

title: Explore data interactively — eda_explore
code: eda_explore(data = NULL, viewer = c("pane", "browser", "dialog"))

title: Explore data interactively — eda_explore
text: Invisibly, closed "Done": list plot (ggplot), describe (eda_describe() output) code (character, code reproduce ). NULL variables selected.

title: Explore data interactively — eda_explore
text: gadget lists data frames seg_cluster() outputs global environment. seg_cluster seg_cluster_set, original data clustered respondents shown cluster solution available grouping variable (e.g. cluster_k4), see eda_describe(). Requires packages shiny, bslib DT; ggstatsplot optional.

text: Plots several variables , optionally group (e.g. cluster solution) weighted: bar charts means error bars, boxplots, stacked bar charts frequency distributions. Variables shown variable labels.

code: eda_plot(   data,   vars,   group = NULL,   weight = NULL,   type = c("auto", "bar", "box", "stacked"),   orientation = c("horizontal", "vertical"),   error = c("ci", "se", "sd", "none"),   conf_level = 0.95,   total = FALSE,   facet = FALSE,   show_values = TRUE,   show_sig = FALSE,   reference = c("total", "rest", "meandev", "groups"),   test_method = c("parametric", "nonparametric"),   alpha = 0.05,   axis_labels = c("label", "name", "both"),   label_width = NULL,   digits = 1,   min_labels = 5,   title = NULL )

title: Exploratory data analysis: plot several variables in one plot — eda_plot
text: data data frame, typically haven-labelled tibble, output seg_cluster() (see "Grouping cluster solution"). vars variables describe: character vector names tidyselect expression, e.g. dplyr::starts_with("F50_0_"). group Optional. Name grouping variable (e.g. "cluster_k4"). Respondents missing group excluded. weight Optional. Name weight variable. type "auto" (default), "bar" (means), "box" (boxplots) "stacked" (frequency distributions). See "Details". orientation "horizontal" (default) "vertical" bars. error Error bars bar charts: "ci" (confidence interval, default), "se" (standard error), "sd" (standard deviation) "none". conf_level Confidence level confidence intervals. Defaults 0.95. total TRUE group given, "Total" group respondents added. Defaults FALSE. facet TRUE, variable shown panel free axes (useful variables different scales). Defaults FALSE. show_values TRUE (default), means percentages printed bars. show_sig TRUE, significant group differences marked (bar charts boxplots group). Defaults FALSE. See "Significant differences". reference "total" (default), "rest", "meandev" "groups". See "Significant differences". test_method "parametric" (default) "nonparametric". See "Significant differences". alpha Significance level show_sig. Defaults 0.05. axis_labels Labels variables: "label" (variable label, default), "name" (variable name) "". label_width Maximum number characters per line variable labels. Defaults 40 horizontal 15 vertical plots. digits Number decimals values bars. Defaults 1. min_labels Minimum number value labels distinct values variable treated numeric (treat_as = "auto"). Defaults 5. title Optional plot title.

title: Exploratory data analysis: test group differences of several variables — eda_test
text: variable differ groups? method = "parametric" (default): one-way analysis variance (ANOVA, F-test linear model variable ~ group; weighted least squares weight given). Effect size: eta squared (effectsize::eta_squared()), share variance explained groups, confidence interval. method = "nonparametric": Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test (stats::kruskal.test()), compares distributions ranks instead means robust outliers skewed ordinal data. Effect size: rank epsilon squared (effectsize::rank_epsilon_squared()). Weights ignored.

title: Exploratory data analysis: test group differences of several variables — eda_test
text: groups differ reference? comparisons linear contrasts group means one linear model variable ~ group, estimated modelbased::estimate_contrasts(): standard errors heteroscedasticity-consistent (vcov = "HC3"), groups may different variances (Welch's t-test). contrast tested t-test (degrees freedom: residual degrees freedom model). weight given, model fitted weighted least squares, group means total weighted. p-values adjusted number comparisons within variable (p_adjust, default Holm), reported p_adj. reference (reference) defines contrasts: "total" (default): group vs. total including group, .e. (weighted) mean respondents, shown "Total" bar eda_plot(). contrast \(\bar{y}_g - \sum_k p_k \bar{y}_k\), \(p_k\) (weighted) share group \(k\). standard error accounts group part total; simple two-sample test group total wrongly treat independent samples. "rest": group vs. rest sample (respondents group). \(\bar{y}_g - \bar{y}_{total} = (1 - p_g)(\bar{y}_g   - \bar{y}_{rest})\), test exactly t- p-values "total"; reported difference larger. "meandev": group vs. unweighted mean group means (deviation "effect" coding, comparison = "meandev" modelbased::estimate_contrasts()). Every group counts equally, regardless size. equals "total" groups size. "groups": pairs groups (comparison = "pairwise"). method = "nonparametric", contrasts computed ranks variable (rank-transformation approach Conover & Iman, 1981), .e. groups compared mean ranks; weights ignored. estimates reported medians, standard errors confidence intervals (rank scale) omitted. direction tells whether group (group1) "higher" "lower" reference (contrast means mean ranks).

title: Exploratory data analysis: test group differences of several variables — eda_test
text: Pearson's chi-square test independence variable groups (stats::chisq.test(), without continuity correction). Effect size: Cramér's V (effectsize::cramers_v(), bias-corrected). weighted, weighted contingency table rescaled unweighted sample size testing, weights inflate sample size. comparisons single groups categorical variables.

title: Exploratory data analysis: test group differences of several variables — eda_test
text: weighted tests treat weights precision weights linear model. approximation; design-based inference (strata, clusters, calibration weights), use survey package. Many tests (many variables groups) increase chance false positives; p-values adjusted within variable, across variables. detailed plot single variable tests (e.g. robust Bayesian), see eda_plot_detail().

title: Exploratory data analysis: test group differences of several variables — eda_test
text: Conover, W. J., & Iman, R. L. (1981). Rank transformations bridge parametric nonparametric statistics. American Statistician, 35(3), 124-129.

title: Assign new respondents to the clusters of a solution — predict.seg_cluster
text: method assigns new respondents way consistent formed clusters (rule = NULL, default): k-means hierarchical k-means ("centroid"): cluster nearest center (Euclidean distance), assignment step k-means. Additional column: distance center. PAM ("medoid"): cluster nearest medoid, using distance measure seg_prep_data(). Additional column: distance medoid. AGNES DIANA ("linkage"): cluster respondent merged first linkage solution: "ward": smallest increase within-cluster sum squares, \(\frac{n_c}{n_c + 1}(\bar{d^2}(x, c) - W_c)\), computed distances (Euclidean distances: nearest center, weighted cluster size), "average", "weighted", "gaverage" DIANA: smallest average distance members cluster, "complete": smallest maximum distance, "single": nearest member. Additional column: distance, linkage distance (Ward scale dendrogram heights). Fuzzy clustering ("membership"): membership degrees minimize objective function cluster::fanny() new respondent, memberships original sample fixed. membership exponent \(r\) \(a_c(x) = \sum_j u_{jc}^r d(x, j) / \sum_j   u_{jc}^r - \sum_{,j} u_{ic}^r u_{jc}^r d(, j) / (2 (\sum_j   u_{jc}^r)^2)\), membership cluster \(c\) proportional \(a_c(x)^{-1/(r-1)}\). respondent assigned cluster highest membership. Additional column: membership_max. Model-based clustering ("model"): posterior probabilities fitted Gaussian mixture model (mclust::predict.Mclust()); respondent assigned probable cluster. Additional column: uncertainty (1 - highest probability). DBSCAN ("density"): cluster nearest clustered (non-noise) respondent original sample lies within eps, otherwise noise (0), dbscan::predict(). HDBSCAN ("density"): cluster nearest clustered respondent original sample lies within respondent's core distance, otherwise noise (0), dbscan::predict(). density rules use distance measure seg_prep_data(). Additional column: distance nearest clustered respondent. Existing segmentations seg_as_cluster() ("centroid"). Two alternative rules can chosen every method: rule = "centroid": nearest cluster center (Euclidean distance). rule = "knn": majority vote neighbors nearest respondents original sample (distance measure seg_prep_data(); ties resolved smallest summed distance). share votes per cluster returned probabilities type = "prob", highest share knn_share.

title: Assign new respondents to the clusters of a solution — predict.seg_cluster
text: Applied respondents original sample, rules k-means, hierarchical k-means, PAM, fuzzy clustering (memberships), model-based clustering (probabilities) density-based methods reproduce original assignment. AGNES DIANA, linkage rule reproduces , respondents (typically 80-90%), clusters formed successively merging groups cutting tree, borders follow simple rule single respondents. rule = "knn" often agrees closely original assignment methods. missing = "mice", passing original sample newdata re-imputes missing values, respondents imputed values may assigned differently. Use newdata = NULL original assignment.

text: measures compare values two respondents: respondents similar answers variables close. Euclidean ("euclidean", default): \(d(x, y) = \sqrt{\sum_{=1}^n (x_i - y_i)^2}\). straight-line distance. Large differences weigh , squared. Use default, particular k-means Ward's hierarchical clustering, built (k-means always uses Euclidean distances, whatever specified ). Manhattan ("manhattan"): \(d(x, y) = \sum_{=1}^n |x_i - y_i|\). sum absolute differences ("city block" distance). Less sensitive outliers single extreme answers Euclidean. Use rating scales, differences one scale point simply add , data contains outliers; works well PAM. Maximum ("maximum", Chebyshev distance): \(d(x, y) = \max_i |x_i - y_i|\). largest difference single variable counts. Rarely useful survey data, single item dominates distance. Minkowski ("minkowski"): \(d(x, y) = (\sum_{=1}^n |x_i - y_i|^p)^{1/p}\), generalization Manhattan (\(p = 1\)) Euclidean (\(p = 2\), used ). Canberra ("canberra"): \(d(x, y) = \sum_{=1}^n |x_i - y_i| / (|x_i| + |y_i|)\). weighted Manhattan distance, differences small values weigh . Use non-negative data (e.g. counts shares, scale = "range" "none"), z-standardized data. Binary ("binary"): proportion variables one two respondents non-zero value, among variables least one non-zero value. Use 0/1 data, e.g. multiple-response questions (scale = "none").
